grid.title: Capillary rise: surface tension of {liquid} ({bore})
grid.unknown: the surface tension of the liquid
grid.method: Capillary rise read with a travelling microscope

liquid.label: water at 20 °C
liquid.note: Clean water against air at 20 °C has a surface tension of 72.75 mN/m and a density of 998.2 kg/m3.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, Surface tension of common liquids and Density of water

liquid.label: water at 50 °C
liquid.note: Surface tension falls as a liquid is warmed: water gives 67.91 mN/m at 50 °C against 72.75 mN/m at 20 °C.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, Surface tension of water against air, 0-100 °C

liquid.label: glycerol
liquid.note: Glycerol: surface tension 63.4 mN/m and density 1261 kg/m3 at 20 °C. It is far more viscous, so the column takes longer to settle.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, Surface tension and density of glycerol at 20 °C

liquid.label: ethyl alcohol
liquid.note: Ethyl alcohol wets glass well but has less than a third of water's surface tension: 22.39 mN/m at 20 °C.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, Surface tension of common liquids: ethanol at 20 °C
